content.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a People Safety & Resilience Manager at GitLab, you'll help protect team members working from home, in Labs, and in coworking spaces. You'll turn GitLab's safety and resilience strategies into practical programs that work across countries, both day to day and when a crisis disrupts how people work.

What you’ll do

Run the occupational health and safety management system in line with ISO 45001. Put the global policy into practice through hazard identification, risk and ergonomic assessments, incident reporting and investigation, performance measurement, internal audits, and management reviews.

Identify and meet each country's legal safety obligations with Employment Law, People Compliance, Benefits, and local vendors. Track changes in the law and keep records of required appointments, assessments, committees, training, and medical surveillance. Manage vendor agreements and keep safety and resilience services within budget.

Coordinate required consultation with works councils and team members before GitLab makes a decision or contacts affected team members outside the consultation process. Prepare consultation materials, participate in health and safety committees where they exist, and retain the consent, hearing, and anonymized reporting records each jurisdiction requires.

Run the workplace violence prevention program. Coordinate the threat management team, train managers, and keep case records and legally required local plans up to date.

Coordinate crisis response and disaster relief. Keep the crisis plan and records current, with a lead and alternate for every role. During on-call shifts, follow escalation procedures and support the crisis team until the response ends. Work with the relief partner to track the Team Member Disaster Relief fund balance and handle communications and reporting.

Maintain continuity plans for the People Group, assess the impact of disruptions, and prioritize recovery of essential services. Keep records for auditors and insurers, run crisis and continuity exercises, lead required reviews after incidents, and track follow-up actions until they're complete.

Assess each requirement in ISO 45001, ISO 22361, and ISO 22301. Each week, review the scores produced by AI agents and correct any errors. Set deadlines for improvements and report quarterly on the safety and resilience measures in the People Safety & Security scorecard.

Lead people safety and crisis response on site at major company events alongside security operations. Confirm emergency procedures and medical arrangements are in place, serve as the crisis team's on-site contact, and lead a review after each event.

What you’ll bring

Experience delivering safety and resilience programs across several countries, covering occupational health and safety plus either crisis management or business continuity.

Knowledge of when to consult team members or works councils, hold hearings, or make decisions jointly, and how to document each step. To handle GitLab's legal obligations in Germany, you'll need direct experience applying the Betriebsverfassungsgesetz and Arbeitssicherheitsgesetz.

Ability to apply ISO 45001, ISO 22361, ISO 22301, the ANSI/ASIS workplace violence prevention standard, and the European Union framework directive on safety and health at work when drafting policies and procedures with legal and compliance partners and external advisers.

Experience managing programs across teams, including assigning owners and deadlines, tracking regulatory changes, and preparing records for audits.

Experience using artificial intelligence (AI) agents to draft materials, score assessments, and update records, and checking their results against the standards. Ability to keep that work repeatable by tracking changes to prompts and workflows in GitLab.

Ability to travel internationally up to 30% of the time to support company events, run exercises, and attend health and safety committee meetings in person. These commitments can fall in the evenings or on weekends.

Availability outside standard working hours as part of a scheduled on-call duty rotation and when the crisis management plan is activated, including evenings, weekends, and public holidays.

Experience managing consultations across Germany, the Netherlands, and France is strongly preferred because you'll work under each country's rules. Safety or business continuity credentials, ISO 45001 or ISO 22301 lead implementer or auditor qualifications, and works council or labor relations training are also helpful.

About the team

We work with Employment Law, People Compliance, Benefits, the crisis management team, team member representatives, and external partners. You'll bring these partners together through plans with named owners and deadlines. Our People Safety & Security scorecard tracks how well we meet safety standards and legal duties and which consultations, exercises, and incident reviews we've completed. It also tracks whether we've reviewed continuity plans in the past twelve months and closed audit findings by their deadlines.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

United States Salary Range

$115,200—$194,400 USD

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being

Flexible Paid Time Off

Team Member Resource Groups

Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan

Growth and Development Fund

Parental Leave

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know during the recruiting process.
